Broadleaf Partners LLC purchased a new position in Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) during the 4th quarter, according to the company in its most recent filing with the Securities & Exchange Commission. The fund purchased 43,664 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock, valued at approximately $7,389,000. Apple makes up about 6.1% of Broadleaf Partners LLC’s portfolio, making the stock its 2nd biggest holding. 
Other large investors have also added to or reduced their stakes in the company. Beach Investment Management LLC. raised its stake in Apple by 1,517.7% during the second quarter. Beach Investment Management LLC. now owns 178,109 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $25,651,000 after buying an additional 167,099 shares in the last quarter. Wedge Capital Management L L P NC raised its stake in Apple by 8,719.3% during the second quarter. Wedge Capital Management L L P NC now owns 384,344 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $55,353,000 after buying an additional 379,986 shares in the last quarter. First Capital Advisors Group LLC. raised its stake in Apple by 1.6% during the second quarter. First Capital Advisors Group LLC. now owns 16,639 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $2,396,000 after buying an additional 255 shares in the last quarter. Teacher Retirement System of Texas raised its stake in Apple by 0.7% during the second quarter. Teacher Retirement System of Texas now owns 3,279,408 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $472,300,000 after buying an additional 24,352 shares in the last quarter. Finally, Smith Asset Management Group LP raised its stake in Apple by 5.3% during the second quarter. Smith Asset Management Group LP now owns 693,701 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $99,907,000 after buying an additional 34,640 shares in the last quarter. Institutional investors and hedge funds own 61.35% of the company’s stock. Get Apple alerts: 
Several analysts have issued reports on the company. Vetr cut Apple from a “strong-buy” rating to a “buy” rating and set a $187.18 price objective on the stock. in a research note on Wednesday, February 14th. UBS set a $190.00 price objective on Apple and gave the company a “buy” rating in a research note on Monday, December 4th. Zacks Investment Research upgraded Apple from a “hold” rating to a “buy” rating and set a $197.00 price objective on the stock in a research note on Thursday, January 18th. Rosenblatt Securities restated a “buy” rating and set a $180.00 price objective on shares of Apple in a research note on Friday, March 16th. Finally, Piper Jaffray restated a “buy” rating and set a $200.00 price objective on shares of Apple in a research note on Tuesday, January 2nd. One research analyst has rated the stock with a sell rating, seventeen have given a hold rating, thirty-three have assigned a buy rating and one has given a strong buy rating to the company’s stock. The company has a consensus rating of “Buy” and an average price target of $201.70. In other news, insider Daniel J. Riccio sold 15,641 shares of the stock in a transaction on Friday, January 5th. The stock was sold at an average price of $174.78, for a total value of $2,733,733.98. Following the completion of the sale, the insider now owns 13,739 shares in the company, valued at $2,401,302.42. The transaction was disclosed in a filing with the Securities & Exchange Commission, which is available through the SEC website . 0.06% of the stock is owned by corporate insiders. 
Shares of Apple stock opened at $168.34 on Wednesday. The stock has a market capitalization of $836,907.75, a price-to-earnings ratio of 17.30, a PEG ratio of 1.25 and a beta of 1.19. Apple has a 1-year low of $140.06 and a 1-year high of $183.50. The company has a quick ratio of 1.20, a current ratio of 1.24 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.74. 
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last released its earnings results on Thursday, February 1st. The iPhone maker reported $3.89 earnings per share (EPS) for the quarter, beating the Zacks’ consensus estimate of $3.82 by $0.07. The company had revenue of $88.29 billion during the quarter, compared to analyst estimates of $87.62 billion. Apple had a return on equity of 37.37% and a net margin of 21.13%. The company’s revenue for the quarter was up 12.7% on a year-over-year basis. During the same quarter in the prior year, the company earned $3.36 earnings per share. sell-side analysts expect that Apple will post 11.38 EPS for the current fiscal year.

The Company’s products and services include iPhone, iPad, Mac, iPod, Apple TV, a portfolio of consumer and professional software applications, the iOS and OS X operating systems, iCloud, and a variety of accessory, service and support offerings.
